structure: Part 6 of repo:frontend read the live-animals set's one review page in full: the check-answers feature folder at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/ — page.js (id/slug/maturity), controller.js (the GET handler, the error summary assembly, the error precedence and which states hide answer errors), template.njk (the whole rendered page: view header, import reference numbers, section loop, summary-card loop, species blocks, groups and the foot form), refusal.js (the Continue refusal rules, unlisted-species errors and document-scan errors), review-href.js (the review URL's staleAction and refused flags), reviewed.js (recording the reviewed concurrency token), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js in full, every file under view-model/ (index.js, view-header.js, species-errors.js, invalid-parties.js, applicability.js, incomplete-cards.js; sections/about-consignment.js, description-of-goods.js, transport-and-arrival.js, documents.js, addresses.js, contact-address.js; cards/documents.js, cards/consignment/origin-of-import.js, what-are-you-importing.js, main-import-reason.js, additional-details.js, commodity-cards.js, cards/consignment/species/species-block.js, identification-details-table.js, identifier-columns.js, cards/movement/arrival-details.js, transport-details.js, cards/addresses/consignment-addresses.js, contact-address.js; rows/change-link.js, summary-row.js, value-text.js, party-row.js) and all 1,685 lines of check-answers.fit.spec.js. It covers the review page's route and maturity, its heading and title in every notification state, the view header (status tag, date line, Amend/Copy as new/Delete, import reference numbers), the six numbered sections and their anchors, every card and every row with its key, value formatting, change-link target and link text, the incomplete-card treatment and all ten Complete messages, the species and party error restatements, the invalid-party case, the Continue refusal rules and the states that hold errors silently, every behaviour the fit spec proves, and key parity between copy.cy.js and copy.en.js. The question pages that capture these answers, the shared layout, error-summary partial and journey strip, the commodities/addresses/documents/transport feature folders, the task rows and the obligations are other parts' and are only cited here where the review page's own files reach into them.

claims.statement: A trader reaches the review page at /notifications/<notification reference>/notification-view, and the page answers GET only.
claims.note: The slug is also the shared CYA_SLUG ('notification-view', src/server/app/shared/kit.js:69), which the change links use as their return marker. The fit spec navigates to `${BASE}/notifications/GBN-0000-0000-0000/notification-view`.

      text: copy.change,
      visuallyHiddenText  /  await expect(page).toHaveURL(
      urlUnderBase('/notifications/[^/]+/commodities')
    )

claims.statement: A read-only review (a submitted notification) carries no Change or Edit details links at all.
claims.quote:
export const editableActions = ({ readOnly, actions }) =>
  readOnly ? {} : { actions }  /  await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: copy.change })).toHaveCount(0)

claims.statement: A row whose answer is blank because it does not apply reads 'Not applicable'.
claims.note: The words 'Not applicable' come from the service-wide shared copy, outside this part.

claims.statement: A blank row inside a card that is carrying an error is shown with no visible text and a visually hidden 'Missing' instead of 'Not applicable', so an outstanding answer does not read as one that does not apply.
claims.note: Blanking applies to the card's own rows and to the rows of its groups.

claims.statement: An unfinished card shows its message as an error paragraph inside the card, prefixed by a visually hidden 'Error:', and the card is given an error style.
The Origin of import card is unfinished when the origin task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete origin of import'; its in-page anchor is origin-of-import.
claims.quote: { id: 'originOfImport', anchor: 'origin-of-import', rows: ['origin'] }  /  originOfImport: 'Complete origin of import'

claims.statement: The 'What are you importing?' card is unfinished when the commodities task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete what are you importing?'; its in-page anchor is what-are-you-importing.
The Main import reason card is unfinished when the import reason task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete main import reason'; its in-page anchor is main-import-reason.

The commodity cards are unfinished when either the consignment details or the animal identification task row is not ready, and then the page reports 'Complete commodity details' against the commodity-details anchor, falling back to the description-of-the-goods section heading when no commodity card is on the page.
claims.note: check-answers.fit.spec.js:1121-1124 and :1266 prove the fallback link target '#description-of-the-goods' on a notification with no commodity line.

claims.statement: The 'Complete commodity details' message is the one card message that never appears on a card, because a commodity card carries no card id to attach it to.
The Additional details card is unfinished when the additional details task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete additional details'; its in-page anchor is additional-details.

The Arrival details card is unfinished when either the arrival details or the transit countries task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete arrival details'; its in-page anchor is arrival-details.
The Transport details card is unfinished when the transporter task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete transport details'; its in-page anchor is transport-details.
The documents card is unfinished when the documents task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete documents'; its in-page anchor is documents.
claims.quote: { id: 'documents', anchor: 'documents', rows: ['documents'] }  /  documents: 'Complete documents'

claims.statement: The Consignment addresses card is unfinished when the addresses task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete consignment addresses'; its in-page anchor is addresses.
The Contact address card is unfinished when the contact task row is not ready, and then shows 'Complete contact address for this consignment'; its in-page anchor is contact-address.
claims.quote: { id: 'contactAddress', anchor: 'contact-address', rows: ['contact'] }  /  contactAddress: 'Complete contact address for this consignment'

claims.statement: The ten review cards are checked, and listed, in page order: origin of import, what are you importing, main import reason, commodity details, additional details, arrival details, transport details, documents, consignment addresses, contact address.
claims.quote:
/**
 * The review page's cards in page order, each with the task rows whose answers
 * it shows and the id the error summary links to.
 */
claims.note: check-answers.fit.spec.js:1260-1294 proves eight of them in that order in the error summary of a new draft (origin and documents are ready on a new draft).

claims.statement: The error summary names every unfinished card, each entry linking to that card's own place on the page, and the same message appears on the card itself.
claims.quote: test('lists every unfinished card in the error summary, each linking to its card with its message on the card'

claims.statement: Where a card id has no place on the page an error entry falls back to a change link to the page that collects the answer instead of an in-page anchor.
claims.quote:
(reviewErrorAnchorHref(key, pageAnchors) ??
            changeHref({ journeyId, changeLinkTrail }, key))
claims.note: mechanism: the set of anchors actually rendered is collected from the sections, their cards and their species blocks (controller.js:49-58).

claims.statement: Only the first card of a repeated card id takes the anchor the error summary links to, so a notification with several document cards still has one target for the documents error.

Where several kinds of error could be reported against one card, the page shows them in this order of precedence: an invalid stored answer, then a document scan problem, then an unlisted species, then an unfinished card, then a species block short of its details.
claims.note: mechanism: later spreads win, so the last-named kind replaces an earlier message for the same card key.

claims.statement: A species the notification still owes a count for is reported as 'Enter the number of animals for <species>', and one that has a count but no identifier as 'Enter at least 1 animal identifier for <species>'.
claims.quote:
noCount: (species) => `Enter the number of animals for ${species}`,
      noIdentifier: (species) =>
        `Enter at least 1 animal identifier for ${species}`

claims.statement: A species error's summary entry links to that species' own block on the page, and following it moves keyboard focus to the block.
claims.quote:

claims.note: The fit spec proves each of two cattle species short of an identifier is named separately and focuses its own block.

claims.statement: Species errors are reported in commodity line order, one per species that still owes a count or an identifier.
claims.quote:
@returns {object} map of per-species key to message, in line order. Empty
 * means no species is short.

claims.statement: When Continue is refused on a draft holding species that reference data no longer lists, the 'What are you importing?' card shows '<latin name> (<code>) can no longer be selected. Select a species from the list.', naming every such species.
claims.quote:
notListed: (speciesWithCodes) =>
        `${speciesWithCodes} can no longer be selected. Select a species from the list.`  /  const speciesWithCodes = unlisted

claims.statement: The unlisted-species message is only ever shown after a refused Continue, and only for a draft — never for a submitted notification or an amendment.
A refusal caused by an unlisted species is logged at warning level with the reason 'unlisted-species' and the lines concerned.
Only commodity lines that have both a commodity code and a species latin name are checked against the species reference list.
claims.quote:
const chosenSpecies = (answers) =>
  toArray(answers.commodityLines)
    .filter((line) => line?.commodityCode && line?.speciesLatinName)
claims.note: mechanism: reshapes the stored commodity lines into code and latin name pairs for the reference-data check.

claims.statement: A document whose scan rejected it marks its card as soon as the review opens, with the documents feature's 'some rejected' message, and the error summary entry links to that card.
claims.note: The message's words live in the documents feature's copy, outside this part.

claims.statement: A document still being scanned leaves its card unmarked until Continue is refused, and only then shows the documents feature's 'still scanning' message.
Opening the review does not re-run a document's virus scan; it reads the status already recorded.
claims.note: mechanism: asks the scan-status helper not to refresh.

claims.statement: Continue is refused when the notification is not yet ready to be checked, or any answered party's address is invalid, or any review card holds an invalid stored answer, or any document scan is rejected or still running, or a draft holds an unlisted species.
Continue is never refused on a submitted notification.
claims.note: A submitted notification shows no Continue button at all (check-answers.fit.spec.js:1377-1379).

claims.statement: A refused Continue keeps the trader on the review page, which then shows the error summary.
claims.quote: test('refuses Continue and keeps the trader on the review page'

claims.statement: A refused Continue on an unfinished notification shows each unfinished card's Complete message on the card and leaves its blank answers blank with the hidden 'Missing', at desktop and at phone width alike.
claims.quote: test('shows the unfinished card with its Complete line and leaves the blank answer with a hidden Missing after a refused Continue at desktop and phone width'

claims.statement: A submitted notification's view, and an amendment the trader has not yet been refused on, hold every answer error silently: no error summary and no card error messages.
claims.quote:

claims.statement: Continue on an amendment with a missing answer reveals the error summary naming that answer's card.
claims.quote: test('Continue on an amendment with a missing answer shows the error summary naming the arrival date'

claims.statement: The error summary takes keyboard focus only when Continue has just been refused, not when the review is merely opened with outstanding answers.

claims.statement: A draft review ends with 'Continue' alone in its last block, with nothing after it.
An amendment review ends with 'Continue', then 'Cancel amend' linking to the cancel-amendment page, then 'Delete notification'.
claims.note: The Delete button at the foot is shown only while the notification is being amended (controller.js:179-180).

claims.statement: A card with no rows shows only its title, any error and its blocks or groups, with no empty summary list.
claims.note: A commodity card is the case: it carries species blocks and no rows of its own.

claims.statement: A card's groups are shown after its rows and after any species blocks, each under a fourth-level sub-heading with its own summary list.
A numeric answer is read back as its digits, and a species block's rows show the stored number of animals for that line.
The 'Main import reason' row's key and the Main import reason card's title are the same words, 'Main import reason'.
claims.quote: mainImportReason: 'Main import reason'
claims.note: Recorded as the source states it; whether a card should repeat its own title as a row key is for the reconciler.

claims.statement: Two row keys repeat the words of the card they sit on: 'Contact address' is the only row of the 'Contact address' card, and 'Type' is the last row of the 'Transport details' card beside the transporter's own name, address, country and approval number.

contactAddress: 'Contact address',
    country: 'Country',
    approvalNumber: 'Approval number',
    type: 'Type'
claims.note: Recorded so the reconciler can see the duplication between a card title and a row key.

claims.statement: The review page carries no caption above its heading: a draft or submitted notification is headed by its reference and a status tag, and any other state is headed by the page title with the journey strip supplying the status instead.
claims.note: Searched the template and both copy files for a caption or section-name key above the heading and found none; the question pages of a section carry section captions, the review does not.

claims.statement: A trader opens the review from the notification's overview, and opens a submitted notification's view from the notification list's View link for that reference.
claims.note: The overview's own review row and the list's View link belong to the hub and dashboard features, which are other parts; this claim records only that both reach this page.

claims.statement: The review is only offered to a trader once the notification is ready to be checked; a notification that is not shows the review but has Continue refused.
claims.note: The readyForCheckYourAnswers gate itself is set by the journey flow, which is another part; the review only reads it.
